chapter: Stuff Smith Trio and New York
title: Just doing the job: modesty, talent and luck
summary: Jones says he never set targets, that music is bigger than he is, and that talent depends on being in the right place.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Yeah. You know, you just go and do it. You just make the record date and make the job and take the money and run, you know? Then, as years go by you realize what you've done. I told someone the other day, I said, 'Gee, whiz, I've been lucky enough to get these accolades in this late stage in my career, but had I thought about it this way I wouldn't have done it that way. I would have started making targets for myself, things to cover, you know?'
Do you think it would have worked better that way, Jimmy?
I don't either. I think the --
Just do the job. I was just so interested in the music, and getting that done, and I had no idea that these pleasant side effects were going to happen.

I had no idea, you know. In fact, I still don't. A lot of people say, "You're too modest." I'm not modest. It's just that music is bigger than I am. You know. It's just like trying to breathe in all the fresh air and reap all the sunshine. It's a great art, you know? Now that's the way I think of it. And I'm so happy that I'm making a living at something that would have been a hobby anyway.
I'm one of the fortunate few.
Well, you also have an exceptional talent.
Well, there are a whole lot of guys that are talented. They just weren't standing on the right corner at the right time. When the right person came around.
